record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: What general properties can be proved about the zero locations, or the relative pole and zero locations, of the Laplace transform of a phase-type distribution? The setting is the Laplace transform of the probability density of a phase-type distribution; known eigenvalue results constrain possible pole locations because poles of the transform are eigenvalues of the generator matrix T in any phase-type representation, but the analogous general information about zeros remains unknown.

evidence.quote: Since the poles of the Laplace transform of the distribution are eigenvalues of the T matrix of any representation
Problem 3: Find general properties about the zero location, or the relative pole/zero location, of the Laplace transform of a PH-distribution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A phase-type (PH) distribution on $[0,\infty)$ is the distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $\{1,\dots,n,n+1\}$ in which state $n+1$ is absorbing and states $1,\dots,n$ are transient. Such a chain is specified by an initial probability row vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $\alpha\mathbf{1}\le 1$) on the transient states and a subgenerator matrix $T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ whose off-diagonal entries are nonnegative, whose row sums are nonpositive, and which is nonsingular (so that absorption occurs almost surely). The pair $(\alpha,T)$ is called a PH-representation of order $n$. The associated probability density function on $(0,\infty)$ is
$$f(t)=\alpha\, e^{tT}\,(-T)\mathbf{1},$$
and its Laplace transform is the rational function
$$\widehat f(s)=\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt=\alpha\,(sI-T)^{-1}(-T)\mathbf{1}.$$
It is known that the poles of $\widehat f(s)$ lie among the eigenvalues of $T$, hence in the open left half-plane, and that for any PH-representation the dominant (rightmost) eigenvalue of $T$ is a real negative number that is a pole of $\widehat f$.

Establish general structural properties of the zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, or of the relative locations of the poles and zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, that hold for every phase-type distribution. In particular, determine which regions of the complex plane can contain zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, and identify any interlacing, separation, or sign constraints between poles and zeros that follow from the PH structure (nonnegativity of off-diagonal entries of $T$, nonpositive row sums, and nonnegativity of $\alpha$).
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a general theorem characterizing the zero locations, or pole/zero interlacing properties, of Laplace transforms of phase-type distributions. While pole locations are well understood via eigenvalues of the subgenerator $T$, no comparable general results about zeros appear to be available in the literature, consistent with the problem being posed as an open question.

status_evidence.snippet: General background on poles and zeros of Laplace transforms; no specific results given for the phase-type subclass.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references discuss poles and zeros in general but do not state structural results specific to Laplace transforms of phase-type densities.
